title: Spaghetti con Bottarga
subtitle: spaghetti with grated cured mullet roe
excerpt: Spaghetti con bottarga dresses hot pasta with grated dried mullet roe, olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, and parsley. The bottarga melts into the oil to coat each strand with a salty, intensely savoury flavour. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Bottarga, the salted and pressed roe sac of grey mullet or tuna, has been produced in Sardinia and Sicily since at least Phoenician times. Spaghetti con bottarga is the most iconic Sardinian pasta dish and a significant part of coastal Sicilian cooking. Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina (1891, public domain in Italy), mentions bottarga as a condiment for pasta. The preparation is extremely simple: the bottarga is grated over hot, oiled pasta and the heat of the noodles is sufficient to warm and slightly melt it. No cooking of the bottarga itself is required. Sardinian bottarga di muggine (grey mullet roe) is the most prized; Sicilian bottarga di tonno (tuna roe) is stronger and more economical.

glossaryTerms.definition: The salted, pressed, and dried roe sac of grey mullet (di muggine) or bluefin tuna (di tonno). It is sold as a whole block or pre-grated. The block grates like hard cheese and adds an intensely savoury, briny flavour to pasta. Sardinian grey mullet bottarga is the most delicate and expensive; Sicilian tuna bottarga is bolder and more available.

content.text: is as close to effortless as a pasta dish gets. The bottarga is grated over oiled, hot pasta: it warms and coats each strand in a waxy, salty layer. Garlic, lemon zest, and parsley are the only additions. There is no sauce to make, no timing to manage beyond cooking the pasta correctly.

The one thing that matters is heat: the pasta must be hot and lightly oiled when the bottarga goes on, and it should be tossed quickly so the bottarga distributes evenly. Do not apply heat to the bottarga after grating; cooking it directly makes it grainy and bitter. Add it off the heat and let the pasta's warmth do the work.

items.prepNote: for pasta water (bottarga is already very salty)

content.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Salt lightly: bottarga is intensely salty and will season the finished dish. Cook {{pasta-dried}} of spaghetti until al dente. Reserve 100 ml of pasta water.

While the pasta cooks, warm {{olive-oil}} of extra virgin olive oil in a large saute pan over a very low heat. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and chilli flakes if using. Cook gently for 2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant but not coloured. Remove from the heat.

Drain the pasta and add to the garlic oil pan. Toss well. Add most of {{bottarga}} of grated bottarga and the lemon zest. Toss again with a splash of pasta water if needed to keep it moving. Add {{parsley-flat}} of parsley.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Grate more bottarga over the top at the table. Do not add Parmesan.

items.cause: Bottarga was added to the pan over heat and cooked directly
items.fix: Always add bottarga off the heat. The pasta's warmth is sufficient to melt and distribute it.

items.cause: Pasta water over-salted, or too much bottarga
items.fix: Salt the pasta water less than usual. Taste the bottarga before measuring: quality and saltiness vary by brand and age.

items.symptom: Bottarga does not melt into the pasta
items.cause: Pasta not hot enough when bottarga added, or grated too coarsely
items.fix: Toss the pasta quickly in the oiled pan immediately after draining so it is as hot as possible. Grate the bottarga very finely, almost like Parmesan.

content.text: Bottarga is a Sardinian and Sicilian product, made on the coastal lagoons where grey mullet are caught in autumn. The best Sardinian bottarga comes from Cabras on the west coast of Sardinia, where the grey mullet roe is harvested and salted by hand. Spaghetti con bottarga is the defining pasta of Sardinia, served in trattorie from Alghero to Cagliari. It is also made along the Sicilian coast with tuna bottarga, which is stronger and less expensive. Outside Italy, bottarga can be found in Italian delicatessens and online. It keeps for months in the fridge once opened, wrapped tightly.
